redaction_note: Non-AOSP package names were replaced with stable com.example.appN aliases so a developer's own apps are not published. Line shape is unchanged, so parsers exercise identical code paths.

fixtures.name: adb_device_not_found
fixtures.description: What adb prints for an unknown serial, using a non-blocking command. Note the prefix is 'error:', not 'adb:'. `adb -s <unknown> shell` does NOT print this -- it blocks waiting for the device to appear, which is why log_monitor validates the serial up front instead of inferring from exit status.

fixtures.name: adb_shell_device_not_found
fixtures.description: `adb -s <unknown> shell` -- the call shape the skill's scripts actually make. The prefix here is 'adb:', where the same failure from `get-state` (adb_device_not_found) says 'error:'. adb mixes the two, which is why adb_exec._classify matches the message body rather than the prefix; recorded so that stays a measured fact rather than a comment.

fixtures.name: am_broadcast_missing_receiver
fixtures.description: `am broadcast` targeting a receiver class that does not exist still prints 'Broadcast completed: result=0' and exits 0. This is why push_notification's success check ('result=' in stdout) can never report failure.

fixtures.name: cmd_notification_help
fixtures.description: Authoritative `cmd notification` subcommand list. There is no 'list channels' subcommand — `cmd notification list channels <pkg>` silently ignores the extra args and runs bare `list`, exiting 0, which is why push_notification always reports 'no channels found'.

fixtures.name: cmd_statusbar_help
fixtures.description: Authoritative `cmd statusbar` subcommand list. Contains no battery-level / battery-charging / wifi-enabled / wifi-level / mobile-enabled / mobile-level / mobile-datatype — the seven subcommands status_bar.py invents. Those are SystemUI demo-mode broadcast extras, not statusbar subcommands.

fixtures.name: dumpsys_activity_anr
fixtures.description: There is no `anr` subcommand of `dumpsys activity`. ActivityManager answers 'Unknown command: anr' / 'Bad activity command, or no activities match: anr' / 'Use -h for help.' -- and **exits 0**, which is the part that matters (see exit_status in this entry). anr_watcher._pull_dumpsys_anr guarded on `returncode != 0`, so the guard never fired; it then fed these three usage lines to a logcat-line parser, which matched none of them. The 'historical ANR pull' the docstring advertised has always been three lines of help text going into a parser that discards them.

fixtures.name: dumpsys_input_method_shown
fixtures.description: IME visibility flags, filtered out of `dumpsys input_method` to the lines matching mInputShown|mIsInputViewShown|mImeWindowVis. Measured on API 33 and API 35: `mInputShown` and `mIsInputViewShown` both exist; **`mImeWindowVis` does not appear on either**, so code keying on it reads nothing. Note the second key shares its line with `mStatusIcon`, so a parser splitting the line on whitespace gets two fields, not one. The full dump is 7000+ lines and names the user's IME, keyboard app and open windows, so it is filtered BEFORE anything is written -- package redaction does not catch free text.

fixtures.name: pidof_not_running
fixtures.description: `pidof` for a package that is not running: **no output at all**, on either stream, and exit status 1. The file is deliberately zero bytes -- that emptiness IS the recording, and the exit_status field in this entry is what distinguishes it from a capture that failed. Any caller that decides liveness by parsing stdout sees the same empty string it would get from a device that is not responding at all; only the exit status separates the two.

fixtures.name: resolve_activity_launcher
fixtures.command: adb shell cmd package resolve-activity --brief -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER com.android.settings
fixtures.description: Correct launcher-activity resolution. app_launcher now uses this; it previously grepped `pm dump` for the first line containing both 'Activity' and the package name, which readily matched an ActivityRecord or a provider (S10, fixed during the adb_exec migration).

fixtures.name: wm_density_after_reset
fixtures.description: `wm density` read back after an override was set and then reset. Only a Physical line remains. Same receipt, for the density the dp conversion depends on.

fixtures.name: wm_density_override
fixtures.description: `wm density` with an override active — emits BOTH 'Physical density:' and 'Override density:'. Needed for a correct px->dp conversion. The override is 480 because it has to differ from the PHYSICAL density of every profile this is recorded on: it used to be 560, which is exactly the Pixel 4 XL's physical density, so the same capture on that device produced Physical 560 / Override 560 and could not show which of the two lines a parser had read.

fixtures.name: wm_density_physical
fixtures.description: `wm density` with no override set — only a 'Physical density:' line.

fixtures.name: wm_size_after_reset
fixtures.description: `wm size` read back after an override was set and then reset. Only a Physical line remains. This is the receipt for the teardown: `wm size reset` prints nothing whether or not it worked, so its silence proves nothing and this capture is what does.

fixtures.name: wm_size_override
fixtures.description: `wm size` with an override active — emits BOTH 'Physical size:' and 'Override size:'. device_utils matches only Physical, so every tap coordinate is wrong by the ratio while an override is set.

fixtures.name: wm_size_physical
fixtures.description: `wm size` with no override set — only a 'Physical size:' line.
